chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he did not accept the testimony of one man against another man, except the testimony of two men against one man.
ai.seo_question: What is the required number of male witnesses for testimony in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'shahadat al-rajulayn' (testimony of two men) as the standard for judicial validity, reflecting the jurisprudential rigor of the Ahl al-Bayt in ensuring evidentiary reliability. It underscores the Shia emphasis on procedural justice, where the burden of proof requires corroborating witnesses to prevent false accusations, a standard that aligns with but distinctively interprets broader Islamic legal traditions.
